The PAUSEWR and PAUSERD flags are meant to stop the cluster from
processing writes and reads
column2: respectively. The FULL flag is set when

column1: the cluster determines that it is out of space
process writes.  PAUSEWR and PAUSERD are purely client-side settings
already implemented in userspace clients. The osd does nothing special
with these flags.
When the FULL flag is set
column3: the osd responds to all writes

column1: with -ENOSPC. For cephfs
layer translates this into EIO.  If a cluster goes from full to
non-full quickly
column2: a filesystem on top of rbd will not behave well

column1: since some writes succeed while others get EIO.
Fix this by blocking any writes when the FULL flag is set in the osd
client. This is the same strategy used by userspace
default.  A follow-on patch makes this configurable.
__map_request() is called to re-target osd requests in case the
available osds changed.  Add a paused field to a ceph_osd_request
set it whenever an appropriate osd map flag is set.  Avoid queueing
paused requests in __map_request()
column2: but force them to be resent if

column1: they become unpaused.
Also subscribe to the next osd map from the monitor if any of these
flags are set
column2: so paused requests can be unblocked as soon as

column1: possible.
